name: Sled Hack Squat
grip: Hands gripping side safety release handles beside the carriage.
description: Squat along a 45-degree angled sled track with back and shoulders supported against padded carriage rests, placing high knee-flexion demand and direct mechanical load on the quadriceps with spinal support.
setup: Load weight plates evenly onto both carriage horns of the 45-degree hack squat machine.
Step onto the footplate with feet shoulder-width apart, middle or lower on the plate according to knee comfort, toes angled slightly outward.
Rest your upper back and head firmly against the back pad with shoulders fitted under the padded shoulder rests.
Extend your legs to unlock the safety handles, keeping knees softly unlocked.
instructions: Lower the carriage slowly by bending your knees and hips, allowing your knees to track forward over your toes.
Descend until your thighs reach at least parallel to the footplate (approximately 90 degrees of knee flexion) without allowing lower back to round or hips to tuck off the pad.
Pause briefly at the bottom stretch.
Press forcefully through your mid-foot and heels to drive the carriage back upward along the rails until legs are extended with knees softly unlocked.
Re-engage the safety catch handles when the set is finished.
cues: Keep back and glutes glued to the backrest.
commonMistakes: Allowing hips or lower back to peel away from the pad at bottom depth (pelvic tilt / butt wink).
Violently locking out or hyperextending knees at the top.
Placing feet too high on the plate, turning the movement into a hip press instead of a quad-focused squat.

logging.example: Four 20 kg plates loaded (two per side): record 80 kg total plate load on sled.
logging.note: Record loaded plate mass; carriage angle (~45 degrees) creates an effective resistance of ~70% of loaded plate mass plus carriage weight.

variantNote: Angled sled machine hack squat with torso supported against backrest. Removes spinal compression and balance limits of barbell squats to maximize quadriceps overload.
